lens: Product systems and reliability — recovery and retry (simulated AI acceptance panel seat)
reason: The Precision Instrument public proposition is clear and visually coherent: student-led consulting, two audience actions, practical engagement expectations and appropriately bounded project proof. The reviewed student journey runs from Join eligibility/preparation into application steps, recovery choice, materials disclosure and submission. Competing copies, revision conflicts and exact uncertain-save retries receive unusually explicit treatment. However, receipt validation is inconsistent at submission, and an irreversible grading-close write lacks an honest unknown-result recovery state. These are interface reliability gaps, not a claim that production data was lost. Supplied local logs support their stated fixture scope; neither source review nor synthetic captures establish observed user success or hosted readiness.

findings.evidence: submit() calls finishSubmission() for every response.ok without parsing the body; that function clears both browser recovery entries and redirects to /applicant?submitted=1. The route contract returns {applicationId} (src/app/api/apply/route.ts:102-112). tests/e2e/application-reliability.spec.ts:64-79 explicitly accepts HTTP 200 with {} as submission success. The malformed-receipt protection present for draft saves therefore does not cover final submission.
findings.userImpact: An empty, malformed or unrelated successful response can dismiss the application and remove recovery without a verified submission receipt. This is a source-demonstrated acceptance gap, not an observed hosted failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate a nonempty applicationId receipt before finishing; treat invalid success bodies as ambiguous, reconcile authoritative submission status, and retain answers/recovery if confirmation fails. Replace the empty-success fixture and add malformed/empty success coverage.

findings.evidence: useRushAction.act() catches a rejected write as only "Request failed", returns false and does not refresh. RoundStatusControl.saveStatus() (lines 60-66) consequently leaves confirmation open with its existing ready summary. A close may already have committed before its acknowledgement was lost. Unlike coverage loading, the write also has no explicit request deadline.
findings.userImpact: After an uncertain irreversible close, operators can still see "Keep grading open" and retry using earlier coverage, without guidance that grading may already be locked. A stalled response can leave all pending controls disabled indefinitely.
findings.suggestedFix: Bound the write wait and represent unknown acknowledgement explicitly. Re-read authoritative round status before retrying, disable close until reconciled, and distinguish already-closed from still-open outcomes. Add a commit-then-lost-response case; existing operator network-failure coverage exercises the coverage read.

notVerified: No staging or hosted integration exists: Clerk session expiry, actual Supabase RPC/RLS, storage transitions and email delivery were not exercised here.
No authenticated live application/operator journey or human usability study was observed. Operator captures are synthetic; source review is not task completion evidence.
Migration/application rollout compatibility, concurrent hosted uploads/submission and operator remediation under real failures remain unverified.
Original-resume access is accurately disclosed in Materials and Review; Board resolution of anonymity policy and retention remains external. Client-approved case-study artifacts/outcomes are absent.
Physical devices, Safari/Firefox and assistive technology were not verified. Supplied log totals were inspected, not independently rerun; no full suite or shared browser was used.
